Um... excited about? Look forward to? Not really. I mean, I used to... I used to joke around with the regulars a lot. Harming myself? Wished I was dead? Um... I mean, I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But sometimes... like when I'm lying awake in bed before an early shift. Those early shifts are brutal. I have to set my alarm for 4:15 AM. I use my phone alarm, but the default sounds are so obnoxious. I had to use a lint roller in the car afterward. Lint rollers are another thing that have gotten so cheap lately. Anyway, what was I... oh, right. Lying awake before the early shift. Yeah, I just stare at the ceiling and sometimes I think it would just be so much easier if I didn't wake up. If the alarm just didn't go off and I could just fade out, so I wouldn't have to keep failing at everything, you know? But no, no actual plan to hurt myself.

Pleasure? Small things? Um... I don't think so. Like, I used to actually get a little bit of a kick out of joking around with the regulars at the restaurant. Weight? Um... I guess my eating has been all over the place lately. Like, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal. We usually get a free meal during our shift, which sounds like a great perk, right? But it's usually just whatever the kitchen needs to get rid of before it goes bad. Last week they made this massive batch of chicken piccata, but they put way too many capers in it. Capers are so weird, aren't they? They're like these little salty green peas that burst in your mouth. I read somewhere that they're actually pickled flower buds. I don't know who looked at a flower bud and thought, "Let's soak this in vinegar for a month and put it on chicken," but it's a very strange concept when you really think about it. Vinegar is another thing—my grandma used to swear by cleaning windows with vinegar and newspaper. She’d save up stacks of the Sunday paper just for that. The ink would get all over your hands and turn them gray. 

But anyway, yeah, some weeks I don't eat the staff meal at all. But then other nights, I'll come home after a long shift and I'll just eat whatever is in the kitchen just to feel settled. Like I'll just stand in front of the fridge and eat cold leftovers or half a box of stale cereal, just trying to feel... I don't know, grounded, I guess. So I don't really know if my weight has changed on the scale, but my eating is definitely just... all over the place.

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Moving slowly? Um... yeah, I guess so. Or sometimes the opposite. People at work have definitely noticed. Like, my manager, Brenda, she pulled me aside the other day. Brenda's been managing that place for like fifteen years, and she wears these really loud, clunky bracelets that jingle every time she points at something. She buys them at those little artisan craft fairs they have downtown on the weekends. I went to one of those fairs once, years ago, and bought this hand-carved wooden owl, but it smelled so strongly of varnish that I had to leave it out on the balcony for a month. The sun ended up bleaching half of its face white, so now it looks like some kind of phantom owl. 

But anyway, Brenda told me I've been acting weird on the floor. Like, sometimes I'll just pace around, checking the same tables and reorganizing the little sugar caddies and looking at the same receipts over and over. But then other times, I just get so... bogged down. Like, just grabbing menus from the host stand and walking over to the POS system feels like I'm moving through molasses, and it takes me way longer than it should. It's like my body just forgets how to move at a normal speed.

He's out there with a leaf blower every single morning at 7 AM. \n\nBut anyway, yeah, I just feel like every small mistake I make at work proves I’m completely useless and just... deserve whatever bad stuff happens to me. I'm waiting tables right now, and the other day I accidentally dropped a tray of water glasses. The ice went everywhere, under the booths... and they have that really cheap carpeting in the dining room that takes forever to dry. It smells like old soup when it gets wet. I don't know why the owner doesn't just put in hardwood or tile, it would be so much easier to sweep up at closing time. We're always there an extra hour just vacuuming. So, yeah... I don't know.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been feeling like you're useless and deserving of bad things?\n\nPatient: Well, the really depressed, guilty feelings... I'd say it's been about a year and two months of feeling like this. Which, actually, is exactly when they hired the new manager at the restaurant. Gary. He's the one who decided we all needed to wear these awful polyester uniforms instead of just our own black shirts. Polyester doesn't breathe at all, you know? Especially when you're carrying hot plates back and forth from the kitchen all night. \n\nThe kitchen is always like eighty-five degrees anyway because the ventilation hood above the fryers has been making this horrible rattling noise and barely working since Thanksgiving. The repair guy came out once, looked at it with a flashlight for maybe five minutes, and said he needed to order a special part from Germany or something. That was months ago. I bet he never even ordered it, he just wanted the call-out fee. But yeah... it's been about a year and two months of just feeling completely worthless like that.\n\nDoctor: Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: Um, pleasure? No, not really. I mean, most days there's just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Just carrying plates, smiling at customers because I'm supposed to, not because I actually feel anything good. Which is hard, because you have to smile for tips. \n\nAnd tips have been terrible lately, honestly. Ever since they started doing that construction on 4th Street, people just don't want to deal with the parking. They blocked off the whole right lane, and those orange barrels have been sitting there for three weeks. I saw a guy in a delivery truck clip one of them the other day and it rolled all the way down the hill into the intersection. The city planning in this town is just a joke. They repaved Elm Street last year and it already has potholes big enough to swallow a tire. My buddy Dave hit one in his Civic and bent the rim. He had to pay like three hundred dollars to get it fixed, and the city wouldn't even reimburse him. But yeah, I just... I don't really enjoy much of anything anymore. It's just empty.\n\nDoctor: Are there any activities that you still look forward to or feel excited about?\n\nPatient: Um... excited about? Look forward to? Not really. I mean, I used to... I used to joke around with the regulars a lot. We had this one guy, Mr. Henderson, who came in every Tuesday and ordered the exact same thing—meatloaf with extra gravy, but the gravy had to be in a separate little boat, not touching the meat. He was so particular about it. One time the new cook, Ricky, just poured it all over the top, and Mr. Henderson actually sent it back. Ricky got so mad, he threw his spatula at the wall and it left this grease stain that's still there. The owner tried to scrub it off with bleach, but it just sort of smeared it around and made the paint look lighter in that one spot. It's a weird shade of yellow anyway, kind of like old mustard.\n\nBut yeah, I don't... I don't really do that anymore. Joke around, I mean. He lives out in Denver now. They get so much snow out there. He sent me a picture last winter where the snow was literally up to his porch light. I don't know how people deal with that. I hate shoveling. It wrecks your lower back, and those ergonomic shovels they sell at the hardware store are a complete rip-off. They're like forty bucks and the plastic cracks the second you hit a piece of ice. \n\nAnyway, I just let his messages sit now. I see them pop up on my phone, but I just... I don't feel the pull to answer them. So, no, I don't really look forward to anything.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel nervous or on edge?\n\nPatient: Nervous? Or on edge? Um... no, I wouldn't say I feel nervous. I just feel... heavy. And tired. Though, speaking of being on edge, you should see the new hostess we hired last week, Sarah. She is constantly pacing back and forth by the front door like she's waiting for the health inspector to walk in. Which, honestly, wouldn't be the worst thing because the walk-in cooler has been holding at like forty-two degrees instead of under forty. The plastic receiver is all cracked because Ricky dropped it on the tile floor back in March. Tile floors in restaurants are the worst, by the way. It chafes so bad. \n\nBut yeah, I don't really feel nervous myself. Just... flat, I guess. I don't have the energy to be on edge.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel any kind of happiness or joy?\n\nPatient: Happiness? Joy? Um... no. Like I was saying before, most days there's just this... this heavy, empty feeling right here in my chest. It's just like I'm going through the motions, you know? Carrying the plates, smiling at people because I'm supposed to, but there's no actual good feeling behind it. \n\nWhich reminds me, I actually broke a plate yesterday. It was one of the big oval ones we use for the fisherman's platter. They're so heavy, and the dishwasher, Hector, he always stacks them too high on the rack. I can hear the bass bleeding through his earbuds all the way from the prep station. I don't know how he doesn't have permanent hearing damage. My uncle listened to loud music his whole life, and now he has to wear these tiny little hearing aids that cost him like four grand. He lost one in his yard once while he was raking leaves, and we spent three hours crawling around in the grass looking for it. We never found it. He thinks a squirrel took it. \n\nBut yeah, joy? No. I don't feel anything good. I'm just smiling because it's my job.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever thought about harming yourself or wished you were dead?\n\nPatient: Harming myself? Wished I was dead? Um... I mean, I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But sometimes... like when I'm lying awake in bed before an early shift. Those early shifts are brutal. I have to set my alarm for 4:15 AM. I use my phone alarm, but the default sounds are so obnoxious. I tried changing it to the harp sound, thinking it would be more peaceful, but now I just associate harps with pure dread. \n\nHave you ever actually seen a harp up close? They have so many strings, like forty-something strings, and I don't understand how anyone remembers which one is which. I went to an orchestra concert once when I was in college, for a music appreciation credit, and the harpist just sat there for like twenty minutes not playing anything, just waiting for her one part. It seemed incredibly boring. The seats in that auditorium were terrible, too—that scratchy red velvet that makes your back sweat and leaves little fuzzies all over your shirt. I had to use a lint roller in the car afterward. Lint rollers are another thing that have gotten so cheap lately. Yeah, I just stare at the ceiling and sometimes I think it would just be so much easier if I didn't wake up. If the alarm just didn't go off and I could just fade out, so I wouldn't have to keep failing at everything, you know? But no, no actual plan to hurt myself.\n\nDoctor: Do you often think about death or dying?\n\nPatient: Death? Dying? I mean, I think I just said... like, I don't sit around planning how to do it. I don't have a plan to hurt myself. But yeah, it's just that feeling when I'm lying there in the dark, staring at the ceiling before my alarm goes off. The ceiling in my bedroom has those little popcorn bumps on it. They painted over it before I moved in, but they did a terrible job, so there are these weird flat spots where the roller pressed too hard. \n\nMy landlord, Mr. Henderson, he refuses to hire actual professionals for anything. He tried to fix the leaky faucet in my kitchen himself last month and ended up breaking the valve, so the water had to be shut off for two whole days. I had to shower at the gym. And I hate the gym showers. The water pressure is like a pressure washer, and the soap dispensers are always empty or filled with this pink stuff that smells like industrial floor cleaner. It reminds me of the cleaner we use at the restaurant for the grease traps. That smell just sticks to your skin for hours, no matter how hard you scrub.\n\nBut yeah, when I'm just lying there, looking at that ceiling... I just think about how much easier it would be if I just didn't wake up. If I could just... stop. Stop having to go to work, stop having to keep trying and failing at everything. It just feels like it would be a relief, you know? But I don't have a plan to make it happen.\n\nDoctor: Are there any small things that still bring you a little bit of pleasure?\n\nPatient: Pleasure? Small things? Um... I don't think so. Like, I used to actually get a little bit of a kick out of joking around with the regulars at the restaurant. There's this one guy, Mr. Abernathy, who comes in every Tuesday and orders the meatloaf. He always asks for extra gravy on the side, but then he never even touches it. It just sits there congealing in the little metal ramekin. Those ramekins are a total nightmare to wash, by the way. If the gravy dries out, it turns into actual cement. You have to soak them in boiling water for like an hour, and the hot water at the restaurant takes forever to kick in. You turn the knob and just stand there freezing your hands off while you wait. \n\nBut yeah, I used to joke with him about it. And I used to text my brother as soon as my shift was over, just to vent or whatever. My brother lives out in Colorado now, and he's always sending me pictures of his hikes. It looked exactly like a ski boot. I really don't understand how anyone is supposed to drive a car wearing one of those things. The pedals are so close together. \n\nAnyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, I don't really get pleasure from those things anymore. Now I mostly just keep my face straight at work. I see the notification, but I just don't feel the pull to answer him at all. I just don't have the energy for it.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?\n\nPatient: Weight? Um... I guess my eating has been all over the place lately. Capers are so weird, aren't they? They're like these little salty green peas that burst in your mouth. I read somewhere that they're actually pickled flower buds. I don't know who looked at a flower bud and thought, \"Let's soak this in vinegar for a month and put it on chicken,\" but it's a very strange concept when you really think about it. Voices? Um... yeah, actually. Sometimes I do. It usually happens when I'm closing up the restaurant, or just sitting alone in my condo. I'll hear this low voice say my name, or whisper that I'm going to lose everything. It sounds so real that I actually turn around to check if someone's there.

I usually buy the fabric ones, but I must have grabbed the wrong box at the pharmacy. The pharmacy is always so chaotic anyway, with the fluorescent lights buzzing and people coughing everywhere. I always feel like I'm going to catch something just standing in line. 

But yeah, the voice... it just whispers that I'm going to lose it all. And it sounds like it's right right behind me.

Well, yeah, like I was saying before, the voices are definitely there. And the thing is, during those really awful, heavy stretches where I'm just so depressed I can barely move, the whispering is still happening at the same time.
